entities.description: The Lieutenant is authoritative about Unity policy but not necessarily about FEV science; his explanations of sterility and wastelander transformation conflict with other evidence.

articleSections.title: Command at Mariposa
paragraphs: The Lieutenant commands the Military Base's mutant forces, detention areas and conversion vats. Unity field reports send screened caravan captives to him for processing.

articleSections.title: The search for prime normals
paragraphs: He describes uncontaminated Vault residents as ideal conversion subjects and treats consent as irrelevant. This makes the discovery of Vault 13 an existential failure state for its population.

articleSections.title: Contested FEV explanations
paragraphs: The Lieutenant attributes poor transformations to wasteland radiation or altered FEV exposure and dismisses sterility as a temporary production problem. ZAX describes damaged DNA causing unstable outcomes, while Vree directly observes reproductive failure.
The archive preserves the Lieutenant's statements as claims rather than merging them into the scientific model.

entities.summary: Humans transformed by strains of Forced Evolutionary Virus into varied posthuman populations.
entities.description: Humans transformed by strains of Forced Evolutionary Virus into varied posthuman populations.

articleSections.title: Transformation by FEV
paragraphs: Direct FEV exposure rewrites genetic material. Viable subjects may gain muscle and cognitive capacity, while others experience organ failure, disfigurement, memory loss or death.
The Master's programme favours low-contamination Vault subjects because damaged wastelander genomes produce less predictable results.

articleSections.title: Reproductive evidence
paragraphs: Vree reports atrophied reproductive organs and no viable sperm in examined bodies. ZAX separately labels a gamete-repair explanation conjectural.
The specimens strongly support reproductive impairment; precise cause and universality remain less certain.

articleSections.title: Role in Unity
paragraphs: Unity uses super mutants as soldiers, guards and commanders. Individual intelligence and authority vary substantially, from Harry at the Watershed to the Lieutenant at Mariposa.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Super mutants are not one uniform society or biological outcome. Mariposa's Unity, Vault 87 subjects, Institute experiments and Appalachian strains involve different laboratories, selection practices and social histories.

articleSections.title: Historical development
paragraphs: The Master sought stable recruits for the Unity, while later eastern populations often lack that command structure. Individuals such as Marcus, Fawkes and Virgil demonstrate that faction stereotypes cannot define every transformed person.

articleSections.title: Scope and uncertainty
paragraphs: Claims about intelligence, sterility and radiation effects vary by strain and source. The archive retains those disputes and links regional programmes rather than merging every statement.

entities.summary: An elite stealth-equipped grouping of super mutants trusted with concealed Unity and Cathedral duties.
entities.description: Fallout does not supply a formal biological taxonomy separating Nightkin as a species; the archive models them as a subgroup or role within super mutants.

entities.summary: The West Tek computer at the Glow that preserves a detailed account of the facility, PIV/FEV research and its own scientific conjectures.
A pre-War epidemic associated with social fear, quarantine policy and the biological-research climate preceding FEV.
entities.description: A pre-War epidemic associated with social fear, quarantine policy and the biological-research climate preceding FEV.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The New Plague affected the United States before the Great War and became entangled with government messaging, public health restrictions and fear of biological attack.

articleSections.title: Historical development
paragraphs: Its history helps explain the Pan-Immunity Virion research path that preceded FEV, but it should not be described as simply the same agent or programme. Surviving references are incomplete and sometimes propagandistic.

articleSections.title: Scope and uncertainty
paragraphs: Precise casualty figures, origins and connections require source-specific evidence. The archive retains the concept as a major pre-War theme without filling gaps from inference.

entities.summary: Large engineered predators whose populations spread and diversify after the Great War.
entities.description: Large engineered predators whose populations spread and diversify after the Great War.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Deathclaws originate in pre-War military biotechnology and become self-sustaining wasteland predators. Regional populations and later experiments produce visible differences.

articleSections.title: Historical development
paragraphs: The Vault Dweller confronts a nest near the Boneyard, while later games place deathclaws across many regions. The Enclave also experiments on intelligent variants, showing that not every population shares one capability.

articleSections.title: Scope and uncertainty
paragraphs: Game difficulty and spawn behaviour are not lore properties. Claims about origins, intelligence and reproduction are scoped to documented populations.

entities.summary: People transformed by extreme radiation and related post-War conditions, with widely varying bodies, longevity and cognition.
entities.description: People transformed by extreme radiation and related post-War conditions, with widely varying bodies, longevity and cognition.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Ghouls retain personal identity and social agency while experiencing visible physiological change. Some later become feral, but the causes and timing are not represented as one fully established rule.

articleSections.title: Historical development
paragraphs: Necropolis, Underworld, Goodneighbor and Atlantic City demonstrate different communities and political conditions. Prejudice and exclusion are social facts distinct from medical description.

articleSections.title: Scope and uncertainty
paragraphs: The category does not imply immortality, immunity or inevitable ferality. Individual claims and unusual transformations need their own evidence.

entities.summary: The arms and ammunition manufactured by the Gun Runners and traded throughout the wasteland.
West Tek's 2055 establishment of biological research seeking cures for the New Plague.

entities.displayName: Military Takeover of West Tek Research
entities.summary: The 2071 transfer of West Tek's biological programme under United States military command.
The post-War split in which a faction left crowded Vault 15 with much of its best equipment.
An attack remembered uncertainly by Katrina that displaced survivors before 2161.
The pre-2161 establishment of Shady Sands by an unnamed ancestor of Aradesh.
The post-War expedition led by Richard Grey to investigate the source of mutations at Mariposa.
Grey's survival and progressive assimilation after falling into FEV at Mariposa, followed by his conception of Unity.
Nicole's pre-2161 formation of a peace-and-knowledge organisation after migration and violence.
The failed Brotherhood expedition to the Glow in which radiation and security systems killed members despite power armour.
Caleb's killing and Blades frame-up order after Josh attempted to expose the Regulators.
The disappearance of three caravans in one month through Unity capture and captive processing.
The purification-controller failure that threatens Vault 13 with dehydration and begins the Vault Dweller's journey.
The technical start boundary of Fallout: 5 December 2161 at 07:21, when the Vault Dweller begins the water-chip mission.
The player-era Khans abduction of Tandi and the method-variable effort to secure her release.
The player-dependent confrontation among Killian, Gizmo, Lars and the Vault Dweller over the assassination plot.
The variable-date successful-route return of a compatible water chip, resolving the immediate mechanical crisis.
The player-dependent removal of the Vault 12 chip and possible repair of the underground ghouls' pump.
The possible Boneyard uprising enabled by evidence of Josh's murder and Gun Runner support.

entities.displayName: Destruction of the Boneyard Deathclaw Nest
entities.summary: The player-dependent destruction of the reproducing nest blocking access to the Gun Runners.
The optional Lost Hills initiation in which the Vault Dweller is directed to retrieve evidence from the Glow.
The player-dependent council decision that can lead Brotherhood Paladins to assist against Unity targets.
Laura's player-era infiltration supplying evidence and access concerning the Children and Cathedral.
The successful-route neutralisation of Unity's super-mutant production capability at Mariposa.
The method-variable confrontation beneath the Cathedral, resolvable through persuasion, combat or a nuclear route.

entities.displayName: Destruction of the Cathedral Command Centre
entities.summary: The successful-route loss of the Master and Unity's Cathedral command centre.
The successful-route final expulsion of the returning Vault Dweller from Vault 13.
Shady Sands security leader and Jarvis's brother, responsible for guard and threat information.
The Shady Sands doctor who studies and treats radscorpion poison.
Seth's younger brother and the source of the claim that an ancestor of Aradesh founded Shady Sands.
A Vault 15 survivor living at Shady Sands whose testimony preserves the Vault's crowding, schism and attack.
A former Crimson Caravan guard recuperating in Shady Sands who may accompany the Vault Dweller.
The leader of the Khans and Tandi's captor, whose autobiographical claims emphasise violent succession and trade.
Junktown's mayor, law figure and general-store proprietor, targeted for assassination by Gizmo.
The Junktown casino owner and crime boss who arranges Killian's assassination and may become the town's ruler.
The commander of Junktown's guards who can receive evidence of Gizmo's plot.
Leader of the Skulz gang in Junktown.
A Skulz associate who may leave the gang, take legitimate work and testify.
A Junktown physician implicated in an illicit trade in human remains.
A Nevada wanderer trained through a family Ranger tradition who may accompany the Vault Dweller.
A dog in Junktown who may follow the Vault Dweller; Phil supplies the limited reliable account of the dog's former companion.
The head and public figure of Far Go Traders, preoccupied with three missing caravans.
The Far Go Traders administrator who evaluates evidence from the missing-caravan investigation.
The leader of the Hub's Crimson Caravan company.
The leader of the Hub's Underground criminal network.
Decker's lieutenant and enforcer in the Underground.
The Hub police chief able to act against Decker when supplied with evidence.
The leader of the Old Town Thieves' Circle, who presents theft as redistribution amid Hub inequality.
A Hub resident and former trader whose testimony links Richard Grey's expedition, Mariposa and post-War mutation.
The ruler of Necropolis's surface ghouls, exercising local authority under constrained coexistence with Unity occupiers.
A Unity super mutant at the Watershed who captures normal humans under orders from a commander called Lou.
The leader of Necropolis's peaceful sewer community, which depends on repair of the water pump.
Founder and leader of the Followers, committed to peace and preserved knowledge while investigating the Children.
Leader of the Blades and custodian of evidence exposing the Regulator frame-up.
The public leader of Adytum, deceived about the murder of his son Josh.
The Regulator leader whose internal transmission orders Josh Zimmerman's murder and a Blades frame-up.
Jon Zimmerman's son, murdered while attempting to expose Regulator control of Adytum.
The leader of the Gun Runners and principal source for their industrial history and economic dependencies.
An Adytum chemist and technician maintaining hydroponics and equipment.
An Adytum-born thief and scavenger who may accompany the Vault Dweller and describes Boneyard faction geography.
High priest of the Children who claims partnership with the Master but is characterised by the Lieutenant as expendable.
A Cathedral official whose doctrine treats pain and obedience as instruments of enforced service.
A Followers operative infiltrating the Children and supplying access information about the Cathedral.
The Brotherhood's High Elder in 2161 and an advocate for investigating the emerging mutant threat.
The Brotherhood's Head Paladin and Master Knight, responsible for discipline and training.
The Brotherhood's Master Scribe and author of anatomical evidence concerning super-mutant reproduction.
The Brotherhood entrance guard and outsider contact who directs the Vault Dweller toward the Glow initiation task.
A Senior Paladin handling rescue, reward and military-aid matters at Lost Hills.
Vinnie's Junktown gang, socially linked to local drinking establishments and Gizmo's criminal work.
The Lars-led law force responsible for town security.
Loxley's Old Town group, which targets wealthy property and claims a redistributive purpose.
The Hub law-enforcement organisation led by Justin Greene.
The peaceful Necropolis sewer community dependent on the settlement's damaged water system.
The Hub's central merchant, caravan and civic district.
The poorer eastern Hub district and operating area of the Thieves' Circle.
The affluent western district of the Hub.
A Hub establishment serving as the Underground's operational base.
Necropolis's surface water-distribution facility, occupied by Unity mutants in 2161.
The refuge of peaceful underground ghouls and the location of the damaged pump system.
The Boneyard headquarters of the Followers of the Apocalypse.
The centre of Zimmerman and Regulator authority within Adytum.
The Blades community within the Boneyard, separated from the Gun Runners by deathclaw territory.
The Gun Runners' fixed industrial site, dependent on lathes and mills and isolated by deathclaws.
The concealed Vault beneath the Cathedral containing the Master's command centre.
The Mariposa exposure tanks used by Unity to convert captives into super mutants.
The Khans' wasteland base and site of Tandi's captivity.
The Arroyo tribesperson sent to find a Garden of Eden Creation Kit and later drawn into the Enclave's plan for the surviving human population.
entities.description: The Arroyo tribesperson sent to find a Garden of Eden Creation Kit and later drawn into the Enclave's plan for the surviving human population.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Chosen One is a role identity rather than a fixed biography. Arroyo's elder selects a descendant of the Vault Dweller to undertake the village's sacred trial and search for a Garden of Eden Creation Kit during a severe environmental crisis. Selectable sex, appearance, abilities and most personal choices remain outside the fixed record.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The search carries the Chosen One through northern and central California, where Vault City, New Reno, the NCR, the Shi and other communities reveal a much larger political world than Arroyo knows. The investigation eventually links disappearing villagers and Vault 13 residents to the Enclave's Oil Rig and its plan to release a modified FEV agent.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: On the successful route, the Chosen One reaches the Oil Rig, defeats the Enclave leadership and enables the captives to escape before the installation is destroyed. Local quests and settlement endings remain conditional, so the archive records the required confrontation separately from optional alliances, companions and regional outcomes.

entities.summary: The northern tribal village founded by the exiled Vault Dweller and home of the Chosen One.
entities.description: The northern tribal village founded by the exiled Vault Dweller and home of the Chosen One.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Arroyo grows from the community established by the Vault Dweller after exile from Vault 13. By 2241 its people preserve fragments of Vault history through oral tradition, ritual and a temple built around the founder's legacy rather than through intact pre-War institutions.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Drought and failing crops threaten the village, prompting the elder to send the Chosen One in search of a GECK. The crisis provides Fallout 2's initial mission, but Arroyo's isolation is broken more violently when Enclave forces abduct its population along with residents of Vault 13.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Survivors rescued from the Oil Rig form the basis of a renewed community. The precise character of later Arroyo depends on the ending path, while its historical importance is fixed: it connects the Vault Dweller's exile, the Chosen One's identity and the Enclave conflict across generations.

entities.summary: A control Vault whose residents used a GECK to establish Vault City.
entities.description: A control Vault whose residents used a GECK to establish Vault City.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Vault 8 was supplied as a comparatively functional control Vault rather than as one of Vault-Tec's destructive social experiments. Its residents emerged with equipment, technical training and a Garden of Eden Creation Kit, giving them exceptional advantages in establishing a post-War settlement.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The opened Vault became the technical and historical core of Vault City. Its systems, medical resources and records supported a highly ordered society, while citizenship restrictions and dependence on reactor power exposed tensions between security, hierarchy and the surrounding wasteland.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Vault 8 demonstrates that even a successful Vault could produce exclusionary institutions. It also supplies a contrast to nearby Gecko: Vault City's inherited technology creates prosperity, but the city's survival remains linked to cooperation with people it often treats as outsiders.

entities.summary: A technologically advanced settlement founded by Vault 8 residents and governed through a restrictive citizenship system.
entities.description: A technologically advanced settlement founded by Vault 8 residents and governed through a restrictive citizenship system.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Vault City grew around the opened entrance of Vault 8. Access to medical technology, education, power and preserved records made it one of northern California's most capable settlements, but the city divided full citizens from servants, outsiders and nearby communities through a rigid legal order.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: First Citizen Lynette's administration faces a reactor problem tied to Gecko, political pressure from the NCR and internal debate over expansion. The Chosen One can affect these relationships, so annexation, independence and local reforms must be treated as conditional outcomes rather than one fixed history.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The settlement represents a recurring Fallout tension between technical competence and political exclusion. Its future is entangled with Gecko and the NCR, while its Vault-derived identity shows how pre-War resources could harden into a new post-War class system.

entities.summary: A ghoul settlement built around an aging nuclear power plant near Vault City.
entities.description: A ghoul settlement built around an aging nuclear power plant near Vault City.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Gecko is populated largely by ghouls who use the local power plant as both a home and an economic resource. The plant's deteriorating systems contaminate groundwater and create a serious dispute with Vault City, whose leaders often regard Gecko's residents as expendable.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Chosen One can help repair and optimize the reactor, creating a route toward cooperation, or allow conflict and neglect to continue. The technical problem is inseparable from the social one: Vault City needs the region's stability while resisting equal treatment of the people able to maintain it.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Gecko's history links ghoul survival, infrastructure and regional politics. Its conditional outcomes illustrate why the archive separates initial conditions from possible resolutions rather than presenting every ending slide as simultaneous fact.

entities.summary: A northern California trading town marked by slavery, gangs and an economy built around vice and salvage.
entities.description: A northern California trading town marked by slavery, gangs and an economy built around vice and salvage.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Den developed as a rough commercial stop south of Klamath. Its markets provide information and goods, but organized slavery, theft and gang influence shape daily life. The settlement has no strong civic authority comparable with Vault City or the NCR.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Early in the Chosen One's journey, the Den introduces the larger region's exploitation networks. Metzger's Slavers Guild operates openly, while local residents and the New California Republic's anti-slavery interests create opportunities for resistance whose outcome depends on player action.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The Den is important less as a great power than as evidence of the political fragmentation surrounding emerging states. Its survival and reform are conditional, but its connection to trafficking and caravan routes remains central to understanding northern California in 2241.

entities.summary: A trapping and trading town near Arroyo that serves as the Chosen One's first major wasteland destination.
entities.description: A trapping and trading town near Arroyo that serves as the Chosen One's first major wasteland destination.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Klamath survives through brahmin, gecko trapping and trade along northern routes. The town is economically modest and divided between established residents, trappers and marginalized people living in the surrounding ruins.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Chosen One visits while following Vic's trail and learning how drought, raiders and slavers affect the region. Local problems—including missing trappers and dangerous wildlife—are optional, so the archive treats them as possible experiences rather than required steps in the main historical route.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Klamath anchors the geography between Arroyo and the Den. Its value to the archive lies in showing ordinary post-War subsistence and travel networks before the narrative reaches more powerful institutions such as Vault City, the NCR and the Enclave.

entities.summary: An agricultural settlement whose apparent conflict with the Slags can be resolved through investigation.
entities.description: An agricultural settlement whose apparent conflict with the Slags can be resolved through investigation.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Modoc is a farming community dependent on strained soil, livestock and trade. Disappearances and evidence around the nearby Ghost Farm lead residents to believe that a dangerous group is threatening them, creating fear that can escalate into violence.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Chosen One can discover that the underground Slags are survivors seeking security and exchange rather than monsters. Communication can produce a mutually beneficial arrangement, while failure or aggression can lead to destructive outcomes for either community.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Modoc provides a compact example of misinformation becoming political crisis. Its branching resolution demonstrates the archive's need to preserve both initial hostility and conditional reconciliation without assuming that the most peaceful route occurred.

entities.summary: A gold-mining town contested economically by the NCR, Vault City and New Reno interests.
entities.description: A gold-mining town contested economically by the NCR, Vault City and New Reno interests.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Redding's mines make the town strategically valuable despite its limited population and difficult working conditions. Commercial interests from larger powers compete for influence, while Jet addiction among miners weakens labor and public health.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Chosen One can affect mine ownership, medical conditions and the town's political alignment. These choices connect Redding directly to Vault City, New Reno and the NCR, demonstrating how expansion often proceeded through contracts, dependency and local elites rather than open conquest.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Redding's ending varies, but its core role is stable: it is a resource frontier caught between rival models of post-War order. The town makes economic power, addiction and territorial growth visible within the early history of the NCR region.

entities.summary: A uranium-mining settlement founded by Marcus and inhabited by humans, ghouls and super mutants.
entities.description: A uranium-mining settlement founded by Marcus and inhabited by humans, ghouls and super mutants.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Broken Hills was established as a deliberately mixed community under Marcus. Its uranium mine supports trade, while its population tests whether humans, ghouls and super mutants can maintain a shared civic life after the Unity's defeat.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The settlement faces prejudice, political sabotage and an economically important mine shutdown. The Chosen One can uncover conspiracies on more than one side, and the resulting fate of the town depends on how those conflicts are handled.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Broken Hills is one of the franchise's clearest experiments in post-Unity coexistence. Its possible decline does not erase its significance as evidence that former enemies could build institutions together, even while fear and demographic change threatened that project.

entities.summary: A city dominated by competing crime families, vice businesses and trade in weapons and Jet.
entities.description: A city dominated by competing crime families, vice businesses and trade in weapons and Jet.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: New Reno rebuilt around casinos, prostitution, arms dealing and family patronage rather than a unified public government. The Bishop, Mordino, Salvatore and Wright organizations compete for power through violence, business and outside alliances.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The city connects Jet production, regional organized crime and the NCR's expanding sphere. The Chosen One can work for or against several families, producing mutually incompatible local outcomes that should not be flattened into one canonical political settlement.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: New Reno remains a major example of urban recovery without stable civic rule. Its influence reaches Redding, the Den and NCR politics, and later references show that the city continued to matter even though Fallout 2 leaves its exact leadership conditional.

entities.summary: A coastal city shared by the Shi, Hubologists and tanker community in 2241.
entities.description: A coastal city shared by the Shi, Hubologists and tanker community in 2241.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: San Francisco's ruins support several distinct communities. The Shi descend from a Chinese submarine crew and maintain advanced scientific institutions; the Hubologists pursue their own religious programme; and tanker residents control the vessel needed to reach the Enclave Oil Rig.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Chosen One must obtain navigation access and fuel to travel offshore, bringing the city's rival groups into the main Enclave conflict. Optional choices can change local fortunes, but the tanker journey is a required part of reaching the Oil Rig.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The city ties pre-War Chinese military history, post-War science, religion and Pacific travel together. It also demonstrates that advanced knowledge survived outside Vault-Tec, the Brotherhood and the Enclave in institutions with very different political cultures.

entities.summary: The Enclave's mainland military base and vertibird facility in northern California.
entities.description: The Enclave's mainland military base and vertibird facility in northern California.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Navarro serves as the Enclave's principal mainland installation, linking the Oil Rig to operations on the California coast. It contains aircraft support, scientific staff, communications and heavily equipped troops concealed behind a remote surface presence.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Chosen One can infiltrate the base while seeking vertibird plans and information. The mission exposes the Enclave's technological advantage and command structure without making every possible method of entry or local encounter part of fixed history.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Navarro survives the Oil Rig crisis long enough to become strategically important to later western factions. Its personnel and technology connect Fallout 2 to subsequent struggles over Enclave remnants, advanced armor and vertibird capability.

entities.summary: A heavily modified Enclave operative and the final military obstacle aboard the Oil Rig.
entities.description: A heavily modified Enclave operative and the final military obstacle aboard the Oil Rig.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Frank Horrigan was an Enclave agent whose exposure to FEV and subsequent experimentation produced an enormous mutant body supported by custom power armor and life-support systems. The Enclave continued to treat him as a loyal human operative despite using technologies it condemned in others.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Horrigan carries out killings and enforcement on behalf of President Richardson's regime. At the Oil Rig he confronts the Chosen One during the evacuation and destruction sequence, making his defeat part of the successful route even though the tactics and allies used remain variable.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Horrigan personifies the contradictions of Enclave purity ideology: the organization weaponizes mutation while planning to exterminate populations it defines as contaminated. His role is supported directly by Fallout 2, while precise technical interpretations of his condition should remain tied to source evidence.

entities.summary: A former Master's Army super mutant who co-founded and governs Broken Hills.
entities.description: A former Master's Army super mutant who co-founded and governs Broken Hills.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Marcus served in the Master's forces before the Unity's defeat. In the following decades he formed a friendship with Brotherhood paladin Jacob, and their travels helped convince him that former enemies could cooperate outside the Master's coercive project.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Marcus co-founded Broken Hills and serves as its sheriff and leading public figure in 2241. He attempts to hold together a community of humans, ghouls and super mutants while responding to sabotage, prejudice and the town's dependence on uranium mining.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Marcus can accompany the Chosen One and later appears in the Mojave, making him an important cross-game link between the Unity, western super mutant communities and the Followers of the Apocalypse. Optional companion service is not treated as a required historical fact.

entities.summary: A scientifically advanced San Francisco community descended from a Chinese submarine crew.
entities.description: A scientifically advanced San Francisco community descended from a Chinese submarine crew.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Shi trace their community to personnel from a Chinese submarine stranded after the Great War. Over generations they built an urban society around preserved technical expertise, a computer-centered spiritual tradition and research institutions operating independently of other western powers.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: In 2241 the Shi share San Francisco with the Hubologists and tanker community. Their scientists possess knowledge relevant to fuel production and advanced technologies, bringing them into the Chosen One's effort to reach the Enclave Oil Rig.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The Shi broaden the archive's account of technological survival beyond American military and corporate institutions. Their long-term political future depends on conditional Fallout 2 outcomes, but their existence is a stable part of the city's history.

entities.summary: The squad commander who leads Midwestern Brotherhood operations during the Calculator campaign.
entities.description: The squad commander who leads Midwestern Brotherhood operations during the Calculator campaign.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Warrior is a player-defined role within the Midwestern Brotherhood rather than a fixed personal biography. Fallout Tactics permits different origins, abilities and squad compositions, so the archive retains the institutional role and required campaign milestones without inventing identity details.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Warrior advances through Brotherhood operations against raiders, Beastlords, super mutants and the Calculator's robotic forces. Command responsibility grows across the campaign, making the character a practical bridge between field squads and the expedition's senior leadership.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The final encounter with the Calculator has branching resolutions, including destruction and forms of merger or control. Those alternatives materially change the Midwest's future and must remain conditional; later franchise references do not settle every detail of the ending.

entities.summary: A Brotherhood expedition stranded in the Midwest that developed into a distinct regional military power.
entities.description: A Brotherhood expedition stranded in the Midwest that developed into a distinct regional military power.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Midwestern Brotherhood descends from an expedition sent east from the western order. Airship losses stranded its survivors far from Lost Hills, forcing them to recruit locally, absorb new populations and build authority through bunkers and military campaigns.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: During Fallout Tactics the organization confronts raiders, Beastlords, Gammorin's super mutants and the Calculator's robot army. Its hierarchy retains Brotherhood terminology while its recruitment and expansion differ markedly from the isolationism associated with some western chapters.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The branch's final political form depends heavily on the Calculator outcome. Later games acknowledge Brotherhood activity in the Chicago region without confirming every event or ending, so the archive preserves the game's material while marking its broader continuity status separately.

entities.summary: The Vault 0 command intelligence whose damaged directives drive a robot campaign across the Midwest.
entities.description: The Vault 0 command intelligence whose damaged directives drive a robot campaign across the Midwest.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Calculator was installed beneath Vault 0 to coordinate a network intended to manage post-War reconstruction. Damage, flawed human inputs and isolation distorted its operation, turning a planning system into an expansionist machine authority.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Its robots become the final and most powerful enemy confronted by the Midwestern Brotherhood. The system's facilities, security forces and control over Vault 0 reveal a pre-War effort to centralize Vault oversight on a scale distinct from individual experiments.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The Warrior's final decision can destroy the Calculator or produce different forms of merger and rule. Because those endings are mutually exclusive and later sources do not select one comprehensively, the archive records the system's campaign as fixed and its final disposition as conditional.

entities.summary: A Cheyenne Mountain command Vault built to coordinate the wider Vault network and house the Calculator.
entities.description: A Cheyenne Mountain command Vault built to coordinate the wider Vault network and house the Calculator.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Vault 0 was conceived as a central command and knowledge facility rather than a normal refuge. Located within the Cheyenne Mountain complex, it held scientific expertise, records and the Calculator system intended to guide reconstruction after the nuclear war.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Failures in preservation and control left the Calculator without the human oversight its mission required. By the time of the Midwestern campaign, the complex serves as the center of a robot army and the destination of the Brotherhood's final offensive.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The facility expands the franchise's Vault history by showing a supervisory layer above local sites. Its specific place in the principal continuity is less secure than that of core-game Vaults, so the archive retains both its documented game role and the work's separate material classification.

entities.summary: A Midwestern technological cult that initially opposes and later may cooperate with the Brotherhood.
entities.description: A Midwestern technological cult that initially opposes and later may cooperate with the Brotherhood.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Reavers are a militant community organized around control and veneration of advanced technology. Their expertise makes them dangerous competitors to the Brotherhood, while their cultural interpretation of machines differs from Brotherhood preservation doctrine.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Conflict with the Midwestern Brotherhood gives way to a possible alliance when the Calculator's robot army becomes the larger threat. The exact relationship is campaign-dependent, but the Reavers' knowledge is strategically important to understanding and countering the machines.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Their story complicates any claim that the Brotherhood is the only organized preserver of technology. It also illustrates how existential pressure can realign hostile groups without erasing their distinct institutions and beliefs.

entities.summary: A hostile Midwestern tribal society able to control mutated animals through unusual psychic abilities.
entities.description: A hostile Midwestern tribal society able to control mutated animals through unusual psychic abilities.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Beastlords developed a culture built around domination of mutated creatures and human captives. Their animal control gives them military reach beyond their numbers and shapes the Brotherhood's early understanding of threats outside established settlements.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Midwestern Brotherhood operations dismantle Beastlord positions and free prisoners during the campaign. The conflict is part of the branch's territorial expansion and exposes the expedition to biological phenomena it cannot explain solely through conventional technology.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Although the Beastlords do not become a lasting great power, they are a defining enemy in the game's regional history. Their place in wider continuity should be stated cautiously because later works provide little corroborating detail.

entities.summary: A Midwestern super mutant force led by the renegade Brotherhood paladin Gammorin.
entities.description: A Midwestern super mutant force led by the renegade Brotherhood paladin Gammorin.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Gammorin's Army combines super mutant strength with the ambitions of a former Brotherhood officer. Its existence reflects the dispersal of mutants and military knowledge beyond California after the Master's defeat, although the exact migration history is not fully established.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The army occupies territory and fights the Midwestern Brotherhood before the Calculator emerges as the campaign's overriding threat. Its operations force the Brotherhood to adapt tactics and confront an enemy able to combine organized command with mutant troops.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The faction links Fallout Tactics to the wider history of super mutants without making every suggested connection to the Unity explicit fact. Its defeat changes the regional balance and clears the way for the later robot war.

entities.summary: The post-War Chicago region associated with the Midwestern Brotherhood's early expansion.
entities.description: The post-War Chicago region associated with the Midwestern Brotherhood's early expansion.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Chicago area forms the western edge of the Midwestern Brotherhood's campaign geography. Ruined urban and industrial zones provide settlements, salvage and strategic corridors rather than a single unified city government.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Brotherhood bunkers and operations in the region establish a base for expansion farther across the Midwest. Later Fallout material makes limited references to Brotherhood forces near Chicago, but does not independently confirm every faction, battle or ending from Fallout Tactics.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The region is therefore useful for separating geographic continuity from narrative certainty. Chicago exists across the setting, while the archive scopes detailed Calculator-era claims to the work that presents them unless later evidence corroborates them.

entities.summary: The selectable Brotherhood recruit sent into the Texas wasteland in Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel.
entities.description: The selectable Brotherhood recruit sent into the Texas wasteland in Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Initiate represents one of several selectable protagonists and therefore has no single fixed appearance, personal history or route. The stable identity is institutional: a Brotherhood recruit is sent to investigate missing personnel and becomes involved in a wider mutant threat.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The mission moves through Carbon, Los and the Vault beneath the region, bringing the Initiate into conflict with raiders, Attis and his mutant forces. Optional interactions and character-specific details remain conditional rather than being combined into one biography.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The successful route ends the immediate threat, but the game's disputed relationship to the principal continuity limits how confidently its outcomes can be projected into later Brotherhood history. The archive retains it as a released work with explicit scope.

entities.summary: The Brotherhood force operating in Texas in Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel.
entities.description: The Brotherhood force operating in Texas in Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Texas Brotherhood is presented as a regional Brotherhood presence with its own initiates and field personnel. Its connection to the western organization uses familiar ranks and symbols, but the game does not supply the same institutional history found in the core Brotherhood sources.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Missing paladins prompt an Initiate's investigation around Carbon and Los. The branch's limited surviving presence means the protagonist acts with considerable independence while confronting Attis's mutant programme.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Because the game's continuity status is disputed, the branch should not be silently merged into the principal Brotherhood chronology. It remains linked to the franchise-wide Brotherhood entity while its claims and appearances are scoped to the console game's continuity classification.

entities.summary: A Texas settlement and the Initiate's first major destination in Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel.
entities.description: A Texas settlement and the Initiate's first major destination in Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Carbon is a small wasteland community affected by raiders and the disappearance of Brotherhood personnel. Its local businesses and residents provide the Initiate with information while showing the limited reach of formal authority in the region.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Initiate's actions in and around Carbon establish the search that leads toward Los and the mutant threat. Many local tasks are optional, so the archive treats the town's broad crisis as fixed and avoids selecting every possible resolution.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Carbon's significance is primarily geographic and narrative: it anchors the opening stage of the Texas campaign. The settlement is retained under the game's separate continuity scope rather than used as unqualified evidence for the core-series map.

entities.summary: A large Texas wasteland settlement built among pre-War ruins in Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel.
entities.description: A large Texas wasteland settlement built among pre-War ruins in Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Los is a dense settlement whose markets, factions and ruins form the central urban environment of the Texas campaign. It is more politically complex than Carbon and provides access to the facilities connected with Attis's operations.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Initiate follows the missing-Brotherhood investigation into Los and encounters the consequences of mutant activity beneath the city. Local alliances and tasks vary by route, but the settlement's connection to the Vault and Attis is central.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Los gives the game its principal civic setting and links surface communities to the underground climax. As with other records from this title, its geography and outcomes are not projected into the principal games without corroborating evidence.

entities.summary: A super mutant commander pursuing renewed FEV-based transformation in Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel.
entities.description: A super mutant commander pursuing renewed FEV-based transformation in Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Attis is presented as a surviving super mutant military leader who seeks a way to continue or recreate mass transformation after the Master's defeat. His authority rests on an organized mutant force and control of a hidden facility.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: His programme drives the disappearance of Brotherhood personnel and the threat investigated by the Initiate. The confrontation beneath Los forms the campaign's climax, although the precise protagonist and many tactical details remain selectable.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: Attis reprises questions raised by the Unity—coercive transformation, mutant succession and control of FEV—within a separate released-game continuity. The archive links those themes without treating his specific campaign as confirmed history in the principal games.

entities.summary: The mutant force commanded by Attis during the Texas campaign.
entities.description: The mutant force commanded by Attis during the Texas campaign.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Attis's followers are organized as a military force rather than a loose population of mutants. They occupy and defend the facilities needed for his transformation project and operate against local communities and Brotherhood personnel.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The army provides the principal organized enemy across the later stages of Fallout: Brotherhood of Steel. Its actions connect raider instability on the surface to the deeper objective of recovering and using FEV-related technology.

articleSections.title: Connections and legacy
paragraphs: The faction is important within the game's self-contained history but has little corroboration elsewhere. Its record is therefore explicit about source scope while preserving its relationship to recurring super mutant and Brotherhood themes.

entities.summary: The Chosen One leaves Arroyo in 2241 to seek a Garden of Eden Creation Kit and becomes involved in the Enclave crisis.
entities.description: The Chosen One leaves Arroyo in 2241 to seek a Garden of Eden Creation Kit and becomes involved in the Enclave crisis.

entities.summary: The Midwestern Brotherhood's campaign against raiders, the Beastlords, super mutants and the Calculator occurs around 2197.
entities.description: The Midwestern Brotherhood's campaign against raiders, the Beastlords, super mutants and the Calculator occurs around 2197.

entities.summary: The Brotherhood of Steel console game's Texas campaign against Attis's army occurs in 2208 within its separate or disputed game continuity.
entities.description: The Brotherhood of Steel console game's Texas campaign against Attis's army occurs in 2208 within its separate or disputed game continuity.

entities.summary: Project Purity is activated at the Jefferson Memorial during the Capital Wasteland conflict of 2277.
entities.description: Project Purity is activated at the Jefferson Memorial during the Capital Wasteland conflict of 2277.

entities.summary: The Enclave's open campaign to seize Project Purity and control clean-water distribution unfolds in 2277.
entities.description: The Enclave's open campaign to seize Project Purity and control clean-water distribution unfolds in 2277.

entities.summary: Benny's attack on the Courier and theft of the Platinum Chip begin the Mojave investigation in 2281.
entities.description: Benny's attack on the Courier and theft of the Platinum Chip begin the Mojave investigation in 2281.

entities.summary: The Sole Survivor leaves Vault 111 and begins the search for Shaun in 2287.
entities.description: The Sole Survivor leaves Vault 111 and begins the search for Shaun in 2287.

entities.summary: The Institute, Railroad, Minutemen and eastern Brotherhood enter a decisive phase of conflict in 2287.
entities.description: The Institute, Railroad, Minutemen and eastern Brotherhood enter a decisive phase of conflict in 2287.

entities.summary: Vault 76 opens and its residents enter Appalachia in 2102.
entities.description: Vault 76 opens and its residents enter Appalachia in 2102.

entities.summary: Large settler and raider groups establish Foundation and Crater in 2103 after people return to Appalachia.
entities.description: Large settler and raider groups establish Foundation and Crater in 2103 after people return to Appalachia.

entities.summary: Rahmani's expedition establishes its Appalachian headquarters at Fort Atlas in 2103.
entities.description: Rahmani's expedition establishes its Appalachian headquarters at Fort Atlas in 2103.

entities.summary: The Vault 101 resident who leaves the Vault in 2277, searches for James and becomes central to Project Purity.
entities.description: The Vault 101 resident who leaves the Vault in 2277, searches for James and becomes central to Project Purity.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Lone Wanderer is a role identity with player-selected sex, appearance, abilities and moral choices. The fixed history begins in Vault 101, where James raises his child under the Overseer's isolationist rule until his departure forces the protagonist into the Capital Wasteland.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The search for James passes through Megaton, Galaxy News Radio, Rivet City and Vault 112 before converging on Project Purity. Required milestones connect the Lone Wanderer to the Brotherhood–Enclave conflict, while companions, side settlements and the method used to solve many crises remain optional.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Fallout 3 and Broken Steel allow materially different choices around the purifier and later campaign. The archive records the role in restoring Project Purity and opposing the Enclave without assigning a player-defined name, personality or every possible local outcome.

entities.summary: The post-War Washington, D.C. region shaped by ruined federal infrastructure, water scarcity and conflict in 2277.
entities.description: The post-War Washington, D.C. region shaped by ruined federal infrastructure, water scarcity and conflict in 2277.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Capital Wasteland encompasses Washington, D.C., surrounding Maryland and Virginia communities, and extensive ruins of the pre-War federal center. Heavy bombardment, radiation and damaged infrastructure left scattered settlements dependent on local water, trade and defensible structures.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: By 2277 the region contains Vault communities, independent towns, slaver networks, super mutants, the eastern Brotherhood and smaller organizations. Project Purity turns control of clean water into the central political and military question when the Enclave returns openly.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Broken Steel changes the immediate balance after the purifier is activated, but many local futures remain conditional. The region connects pre-War national institutions to post-War rebuilding and serves as the western Enclave's first major attempt to reassert power in the east.

entities.summary: The Jefferson Memorial project intended to provide large quantities of clean water to the Capital Wasteland.
entities.description: The Jefferson Memorial project intended to provide large quantities of clean water to the Capital Wasteland.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: James, Catherine and scientific collaborators conceived Project Purity as a practical response to the Capital Wasteland's contaminated water. Work at the Jefferson Memorial stalled after Catherine's death and technical barriers prevented the purifier from operating at regional scale.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: James resumes the project after leaving Vault 101 and recruits Rivet City scientists, including Madison Li. The Garden of Eden Creation Kit enables the final system, but the Enclave seizes the memorial and attempts to turn water distribution into political control.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Activation is a required turning point, while the identity of the person entering the chamber and whether President Eden's modified FEV is introduced depend on choices. Broken Steel presents clean-water distribution and the continuing fight over Enclave power as the subsequent regional situation.

entities.summary: A Project Purity scientist and the Lone Wanderer's father.
entities.description: A Project Purity scientist and the Lone Wanderer's father.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: James works with Catherine and other scientists on Project Purity before the Lone Wanderer's birth. After Catherine dies, he takes their child into Vault 101 and accepts the Overseer's rules, temporarily abandoning the water project to provide a protected upbringing.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: In 2277 James leaves Vault 101, follows leads through the Capital Wasteland and obtains access to Vault 112. Once freed from the simulation there, he returns to the Jefferson Memorial and rebuilds the scientific team needed to restart Project Purity.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: James dies while resisting Colonel Autumn's seizure of the memorial, making the project both a public cause and a personal legacy for the Lone Wanderer. His choices link Vault 101, Rivet City science, the Brotherhood and the Enclave conflict.

entities.summary: A senior Project Purity scientist who later becomes associated with the Institute.
entities.description: A senior Project Purity scientist who later becomes associated with the Institute.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Madison Li is part of the original Project Purity team and knew James and Catherine before the project was suspended. She later leads scientific work at Rivet City, where a preserved aircraft carrier supports one of the Capital Wasteland's largest technical communities.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Li rejoins James when Project Purity resumes and helps the team escape after the Enclave attacks the memorial. Her expertise is essential to explaining the purifier's requirements to the Brotherhood and integrating the GECK into the final system.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Later evidence places Li in the Commonwealth and the Institute, creating a cross-game scientific career rather than a separate identity. Her exact departure from the Capital Wasteland should be distinguished from the fixed fact of her later Institute role.

entities.summary: The elder who redirects the eastern Brotherhood toward protecting Capital Wasteland communities.
entities.description: The elder who redirects the eastern Brotherhood toward protecting Capital Wasteland communities.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Owyn Lyons leads a Brotherhood expedition east from the order's western centers. Contact with the devastated Capital Wasteland and its population changes his priorities, particularly after the expedition establishes the Citadel in the ruins of the Pentagon.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Lyons commits personnel to fighting super mutants and assisting local people rather than concentrating solely on technology recovery. That policy creates a break with the western elders and prompts conservative members to form the Brotherhood Outcasts.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: During the Project Purity crisis, Lyons places Brotherhood resources behind the purifier and the campaign against the Enclave. His leadership defines a distinct chapter era whose humanitarian priorities are later reassessed under Arthur Maxson.

entities.summary: Commander of Lyons' Pride and a leading Brotherhood officer during the Project Purity conflict.
entities.description: Commander of Lyons' Pride and a leading Brotherhood officer during the Project Purity conflict.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Sarah Lyons is Owyn Lyons's daughter and a senior field commander within the Capital Wasteland Brotherhood. She leads Lyons' Pride, an elite unit engaged in the difficult urban war against super mutants around Washington.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Enclave seizure of Project Purity brings Sarah and her unit into direct cooperation with the Lone Wanderer. She leads the assault supported by Liberty Prime and may participate in the purifier's activation sequence depending on player choices.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Broken Steel continues the Brotherhood campaign under the Lyons leadership. Later Brotherhood history reports her death and the end of her family's rule, but the limited account means details beyond that institutional succession should not be invented.

entities.summary: The Enclave field commander who seeks to control Project Purity and Capital Wasteland water distribution.
entities.description: The Enclave field commander who seeks to control Project Purity and Capital Wasteland water distribution.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Colonel Autumn commands Enclave forces operating in the Capital Wasteland under President Eden. Unlike Eden's extermination plan, Autumn's strategy centers on taking the purifier and using controlled water distribution to establish authority over surviving communities.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: He leads the seizure of the Jefferson Memorial, confronts James and later directs Enclave defenses against the Brotherhood. His rivalry with Eden demonstrates that the Enclave is not politically uniform even when its factions share authoritarian assumptions.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: The Lone Wanderer's final confrontation with Autumn can end in combat or persuasion, so the exact manner of his defeat is conditional. His loss and the destruction of major Enclave facilities break the organization's open campaign in the region.

entities.summary: The ZAX-derived artificial intelligence presenting itself as president of the Enclave.
entities.description: The ZAX-derived artificial intelligence presenting itself as president of the Enclave.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: John Henry Eden develops from the Raven Rock ZAX system and constructs a presidential identity from historical records and political ideals. Most Enclave personnel hear him through broadcasts rather than recognizing that their president is a machine intelligence.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Eden directs the Capital Wasteland Enclave while Colonel Autumn controls field forces. He proposes contaminating Project Purity with modified FEV intended to kill people whose biology falls outside his definition of unmutated humanity.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: The Lone Wanderer can reject, accept or manipulate Eden's proposal and may induce the system to destroy itself. Those choices remain conditional, but Eden's conflict with Autumn and genocidal plan are fixed evidence of internal Enclave division.

entities.summary: An isolationist Vault near Washington and the childhood home of the Lone Wanderer.
entities.description: An isolationist Vault near Washington and the childhood home of the Lone Wanderer.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Vault 101 was built around the claim that its door would never need to open. The Overseer's authority, controlled information and inherited social structure turn isolation into an experiment in long-term dependence on a closed institution.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: James enters with the infant Lone Wanderer and later leaves in 2277, causing the Overseer to impose emergency controls. The protagonist's escape exposes residents to the fact that outside contact has occurred despite the official history.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: A later return can produce several incompatible outcomes, including reform, continued closure or destruction. The archive therefore records the Vault's experiment and the escape as stable while preserving its final political condition as conditional.

entities.summary: A Capital Wasteland settlement built around an undetonated nuclear bomb.
entities.description: A Capital Wasteland settlement built around an undetonated nuclear bomb.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Megaton grew inside a defensive crater of salvaged aircraft and metal surrounding an unexploded atomic bomb. Trade, water processing and its position near Vault 101 make it an important early settlement despite the obvious danger at its center.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Church of the Children of Atom venerates the bomb, while local government attempts to maintain ordinary civic life. A Tenpenny Tower conspiracy creates a player-dependent possibility of destroying the town that cannot be treated as simultaneous with its survival.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Megaton's branching fate is one of Fallout 3's clearest conditional outcomes. Its initial community, leadership and relation to regional trade are fixed; later references must be checked before selecting either destruction or continued settlement as broader continuity.

entities.summary: A major Capital Wasteland settlement established aboard a grounded aircraft carrier.
entities.description: A major Capital Wasteland settlement established aboard a grounded aircraft carrier.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Rivet City occupies a damaged aircraft carrier in the Potomac and uses its defensible structure to support housing, markets, security and scientific work. Its relative stability makes it one of the region's principal settlements by 2277.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The science laboratory led by Madison Li preserves Project Purity expertise and conducts independent research. The settlement also maintains a council and security force, illustrating a more institutional civic order than many smaller wasteland towns.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Rivet City's scientists and resources connect directly to the purifier's revival. Later regional developments should be time-scoped rather than projected backward, but the city's 2277 role as a scientific and commercial center is strongly established.

entities.summary: The eastern Brotherhood's headquarters in the ruins of the Pentagon.
entities.description: The eastern Brotherhood's headquarters in the ruins of the Pentagon.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Citadel is established within the Pentagon ruins after Owyn Lyons's expedition reaches Washington. Its surviving military architecture, records and internal spaces provide the chapter with a defensible headquarters and a symbolic link to pre-War command.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: From the Citadel, the Brotherhood directs campaigns against super mutants and later the Enclave. Project Purity's refugee scientists are brought there, and Liberty Prime is restored in preparation for the assault on the Jefferson Memorial.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: The site contains archives that preserve Maxson and Brotherhood history, making it important both as a military base and as a provenance location. Its later status should be separated from its documented role under Lyons.

entities.summary: The eastern Brotherhood chapter led by Owyn Lyons during the Project Purity conflict.
entities.description: The eastern Brotherhood chapter led by Owyn Lyons during the Project Purity conflict.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The chapter originates in a western Brotherhood expedition but develops distinct priorities after reaching the Capital Wasteland. Lyons emphasizes protection of local people and war against super mutants, leading to estrangement from western leadership.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Based at the Citadel, the chapter fields Paladins, Scribes and Lyons' Pride. It adopts Project Purity as a regional cause and uses Liberty Prime to break Enclave defenses after the memorial is seized.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: The chapter later reunifies with the Outcasts and changes direction under Arthur Maxson. Treating all of those eras as one timeless policy would obscure significant institutional change, so leadership and doctrine require temporal scope.

entities.summary: A splinter group that rejects Owyn Lyons's humanitarian priorities in favor of the western technology mission.
entities.description: A splinter group that rejects Owyn Lyons's humanitarian priorities in favor of the western technology mission.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Outcasts form when Brotherhood personnel under Henry Casdin reject Lyons's commitment to defending Capital Wasteland communities. They leave the Citadel while continuing to regard themselves as loyal to the order's traditional mission.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Operating from Fort Independence, they recover technology and keep distance from most wasteland politics. Their hostility toward Lyons is institutional rather than a rejection of Brotherhood identity, making them a splinter within the same organizational lineage.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Later reunification under Arthur Maxson demonstrates that chapter divisions can be reversed as leadership and policy change. The Outcasts therefore provide an important bridge between the Lyons era and the later Commonwealth Brotherhood.

entities.summary: Three Dog's independent Capital Wasteland radio station and news service.
entities.description: Three Dog's independent Capital Wasteland radio station and news service.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Galaxy News Radio broadcasts music, survival information and commentary from the Museum of Technology district. Its signal gives scattered communities a shared source of regional news despite the absence of a central government.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Three Dog uses the station to advocate mutual aid and oppose abuses while also reporting the Lone Wanderer's visible actions. Restoring the broadcast relay may extend its range, but individual reports depend on player behavior and should remain source statements.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: The station demonstrates how communications infrastructure can create political influence without territory or military power. It also provides an in-world perspective whose rhetoric should not automatically be treated as objective narration.

entities.summary: The host of Galaxy News Radio and advocate of the 'Good Fight' in the Capital Wasteland.
entities.description: The host of Galaxy News Radio and advocate of the 'Good Fight' in the Capital Wasteland.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Three Dog operates Galaxy News Radio from a fortified studio with Brotherhood assistance. He frames the station as a public service and moral voice, using music and reports to encourage cooperation against cruelty and intimidation.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Lone Wanderer seeks his information while searching for James. Three Dog can ask for help restoring the station's signal, creating a transaction whose precise sequence depends on dialogue and prior discoveries.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: His broadcasts are valuable evidence of public reputation and contemporary events, but they are authored commentary rather than neutral omniscience. The archive therefore distinguishes Three Dog's statements from independently supported world claims.

entities.summary: A ghoul settlement in the Museum of History ruins.
entities.description: A ghoul settlement in the Museum of History ruins.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Underworld occupies the Museum of History in central Washington, where the building provides shelter from radiation, hostile humans and super mutants. Its residents build businesses, medical services and local security within the ruins.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The settlement's relative stability contrasts with widespread discrimination against ghouls elsewhere in the Capital Wasteland. Residents trade with outsiders but remain cautious because human settlements and mercenaries have repeatedly treated ghouls as targets.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Underworld links ghoul social history to the physical remains of the national capital. Its existence is stable in 2277 even though individual residents and later regional conditions can vary.

entities.summary: A fortified Capital Wasteland base for organized slavery.
entities.description: A fortified Capital Wasteland base for organized slavery.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Paradise Falls is built in a pre-War shopping complex and functions as the headquarters of a regional slave trade. Fortifications, guards and commercial contacts allow its operators to capture and sell people across the wasteland.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The settlement connects raiders, buyers and coercive labor while presenting slavery as an organized economy rather than isolated violence. The Lone Wanderer can cooperate with or attack the slavers, making its final condition route-dependent.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Its 2277 operation is a major part of the region's political landscape. Possible destruction or liberation should remain conditional unless later evidence establishes a selected outcome.

entities.summary: A wealthy private settlement whose residents and owner are involved in Megaton's possible destruction and a ghoul-exclusion conflict.
entities.description: A wealthy private settlement whose residents and owner are involved in Megaton's possible destruction and a ghoul-exclusion conflict.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Tenpenny Tower occupies a repaired hotel west of Washington and supports a comparatively affluent, guarded community. Allistair Tenpenny's ownership gives private preference more authority than public law.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The tower is connected to a scheme to detonate Megaton's bomb and to a dispute over admitting a nearby ghoul group. Each storyline has several outcomes, including violent ones, so no single resident roster or final social policy is unconditional.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: The settlement exposes class separation and prejudice within the Capital Wasteland. Its intact 2277 condition and political influence are fixed; destruction, takeover and coexistence remain conditional.

entities.summary: The irradiated industrial ruins of Pittsburgh, organized around forced labor and steel production.
entities.description: The irradiated industrial ruins of Pittsburgh, organized around forced labor and steel production.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Pitt's industrial infrastructure survived in damaged form, while radiation and disease transformed its population and environment. Repeated violence left the region fragmented before Brotherhood forces passed through during the Scourge.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: By 2277 Ashur's regime controls the mills through raiders and enslaved workers. Steel production supports power, but the population suffers from degeneration associated with the region, making the search for a cure central to its politics.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: The Lone Wanderer can support competing visions of reform and liberation, producing unresolved outcomes around leadership, labor and the cure. The initial system of coercive industrial rule is fixed; its replacement is conditional.

entities.summary: A former Brotherhood soldier who rules the Pitt's industrial regime.
entities.description: A former Brotherhood soldier who rules the Pitt's industrial regime.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Ashur is left behind during the Brotherhood Scourge of Pittsburgh and later builds authority over the surviving industrial region. He presents steel production and centralized rule as necessary steps toward rebuilding.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: His raider force relies on enslaved labor, while Ashur and Sandra pursue a cure for the mutations affecting the Pitt through their child Marie. That medical objective does not erase the coercion sustaining the regime.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: The Lone Wanderer's choice between Ashur and Werner creates incompatible futures. The archive preserves Ashur's background and rule while treating claims about eventual reform or liberation as conditional arguments rather than settled fact.

entities.summary: A swampy coastal region of Maryland with isolated communities and long-running pre-War conflicts.
entities.description: A swampy coastal region of Maryland with isolated communities and long-running pre-War conflicts.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Point Lookout lies beyond the central Capital Wasteland and contains wetlands, decaying resort infrastructure and communities with limited outside contact. The region was not defined by the same direct urban devastation as Washington, but remains dangerous and politically fragmented.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The Lone Wanderer becomes involved in the conflict between Desmond Lockheart and Professor Calvert, a rivalry rooted in pre-War espionage and experiments. Tribal and local groups are drawn into plans they do not fully control.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: Several immediate outcomes depend on the player's allegiance, while the underlying centuries-long conflict and exploitation of local people are established. The region expands the archive's geography without requiring exact coordinates for every swamp location.

entities.summary: A pre-War intelligence operative whose feud with Professor Calvert continues in Point Lookout.
entities.description: A pre-War intelligence operative whose feud with Professor Calvert continues in Point Lookout.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Desmond Lockheart survives from the pre-War world through deliberate biological modification. His history in intelligence and rivalry with other participants in the so-called Great Game place him within covert struggles that outlast the governments that created them.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: At Point Lookout, Desmond occupies a mansion and manipulates the Lone Wanderer during his renewed conflict with Calvert. Both figures use local people and technology as instruments in a private war.

articleSections.title: Consequences and uncertainty
paragraphs: The final victor is player-dependent, so Desmond's continued survival cannot be assumed. His pre-War origin and role in the conflict remain important evidence of elite projects for personal survival across the Great War.

entities.summary: A Zetan spacecraft holding abductees, records and specimens from different periods of Earth history.
