articleSections.title: Outcomes and interpretation
paragraphs: The archive records demonstrated presence in the Divide separately from speculative regional consequences.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Zion's water, cliffs and plant life support communities including the Sorrows and Dead Horses. Surviving records of Randall Clark shape the Sorrows' inherited stories without direct contact.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: The White Legs invade while seeking status with Caesar's Legion, and New Canaanite survivors help organise defence or evacuation. The Courier arrives with a caravan caught in the conflict.

articleSections.title: Outcomes and interpretation
paragraphs: Evacuation and resistance endings are conditional. The region's communities must not be described as culturally static or interchangeable.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Daniel works among the Sorrows and seeks to protect them from the White Legs. He fears that organised warfare will destroy qualities he values in their culture.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: His evacuation plan conflicts with Joshua Graham's proposed defence. Both positions involve outside influence, and the Courier's decision determines the campaign's route.

articleSections.title: Outcomes and interpretation
paragraphs: The narrative's descriptions of innocence reflect Daniel's perspective and should not be adopted as an objective measure of the Sorrows.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Dead Horses have their own leadership and practices while accepting Graham as war chief for the immediate crisis. Their alliance links New Canaanite survivors to Zion's defence.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Members guide and fight alongside the Courier against White Legs incursions. Their future depends on the broader Honest Hearts outcome.

articleSections.title: Outcomes and interpretation
paragraphs: The archive avoids reducing the community to Graham's command or treating his cultural vocabulary as their complete identity.

entities.summary: A Zion tribal community whose home becomes the central object of the Honest Hearts evacuation debate.

articleSections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Sorrows developed in Zion with stories influenced by caches and messages left by Randall Clark. Their knowledge of the canyon is practical, social and historical rather than evidence of isolation from thought.

articleSections.title: Historical role
paragraphs: Daniel urges evacuation while Graham supports armed defence. The Courier's choices affect displacement, violence and later cultural change.

articleSections.title: Outcomes and interpretation
paragraphs: Descriptions of innocence or corruption are value judgments made by other characters; the community's agency should remain visible.

entities.summary: The player-defined manager role responsible for a simulated Vault in Fallout Shelter.
entities.description: The player-defined manager role responsible for a simulated Vault in Fallout Shelter.

articleSections.title: Subject and scope
paragraphs: The Overseer is an interface role rather than a fixed person with a franchise-wide biography. Players choose a Vault number, assign rooms and direct a population through an open-ended management simulation.

articleSections.title: Simulation model
paragraphs: Objectives include maintaining resources, admitting dwellers, responding to incidents and sending teams into the wasteland. These systems demonstrate Vault life themes without establishing one historical facility.

articleSections.title: Archive treatment
paragraphs: The archive scopes this record to Fallout Shelter's gameplay-forward supplementary continuity. Random incidents, crossover characters and repeated quests are not promoted into unconditional world chronology.

entities.summary: The player-built Vault environment used by Fallout Shelter's management simulation.
entities.description: The player-built Vault environment used by Fallout Shelter's management simulation.

articleSections.title: Subject and scope
paragraphs: A Shelter Vault begins as a small underground facility and expands through rooms for power, food, water, training, production and habitation. Layout and Vault number are player-selected.

articleSections.title: Simulation model
paragraphs: Dwellers work, form families, explore and respond to attacks or accidents under the Overseer's direction. The simulation combines recognisable franchise institutions with balance-driven mechanics.

articleSections.title: Archive treatment
paragraphs: No one layout, population or disaster sequence is treated as a canonical Vault history. The record exists to index the game's central subject while maintaining source boundaries.

entities.summary: The variable population managed inside a player-created Fallout Shelter Vault.
entities.description: The variable population managed inside a player-created Fallout Shelter Vault.

articleSections.title: Subject and scope
paragraphs: Dwellers have names, SPECIAL attributes, equipment and work assignments generated or selected within the simulation. Some resemble characters from other Fallout works through collection systems.

articleSections.title: Simulation model
paragraphs: Population growth and expeditions give the Vault a continuing social loop, but repetition and random generation mean these residents do not form one stable historical cast.

articleSections.title: Archive treatment
paragraphs: Named crossover appearances are therefore metadata about the game, not evidence that every represented character cohabited one Vault at one time.

entities.summary: The archival continuity rule separating Fallout Shelter's management systems from unconditional franchise history.
entities.description: The archival continuity rule separating Fallout Shelter's management systems from unconditional franchise history.

articleSections.title: Subject and scope
paragraphs: Fallout Shelter presents Vault-Tec architecture, creatures, equipment and people through a repeatable mobile-management structure. That structure is useful reference material but is not a conventional fixed campaign.

articleSections.title: Simulation model
paragraphs: The archive can index what the game depicts while qualifying randomly generated rooms, incidents and cross-title character collection. This prevents gameplay convenience from becoming false chronology.

articleSections.title: Archive treatment
paragraphs: Future records should cite fixed quest text or official material where available and retain this scope for simulation-only claims.

disputes.assessment: Myron claims responsibility for Jet, while later released material is commonly read as placing Jet in a pre-War context. The records are shown separately because their scope, narrator reliability and chronology do not support a silent single-answer resolution.

Fallout establishes that Katrina left Vault 15 and lived at Shady Sands, while Jarvis names an ancestor of Aradesh as founder without identifying that person's origin. A wholly Vault 15-derived founding population is not established by Fallout alone.

The diary chronology and transformation sequence make the Richard Grey–Master identity a strong inference, but the archive preserves the distinction between cumulative evidence and an explicit single-source identity statement.
Morpheus presents himself as the Master's partner; the Lieutenant's language places him lower and treats him as expendable. Both source statements remain visible.

Vree reports direct anatomical observations; ZAX offers a conjectural mechanism; the Lieutenant calls the problem temporary. These differ in evidentiary status and should not be collapsed into one claim.
Both sources associate contaminated subjects with poorer conversion, but their explanations and authority differ. ZAX reports experimental observations; the Lieutenant supplies an operational theory.
The cautious-aid and Steel Plague slides are opposed branches. Neither should be presented as an unconditional description of the Brotherhood.
Dehydration, restored survival and mutant invasion are conditional outcomes produced by different world states.

outcomeGroups.title: Junktown endings

outcomeGroups.title: Necropolis endings
outcomeGroups.description: Water restoration, dehydration, and mutant invasion are distinct branches.

outcomeGroups.title: Khans endings
outcomeGroups.description: The gang may be destroyed, regroup, or fall to the mutant advance.

outcomeGroups.description: Fallout supplies selected state-dependent slides rather than an exhaustive result for every Hub configuration.

outcomeGroups.description: Survival and later influence are opposed to destruction during the mutant advance.

outcomeGroups.title: Brotherhood endings
outcomeGroups.description: The cautious-aid and Steel Plague endings are contradictory alternatives, not simultaneous faction traits.

outcomeGroups.title: Master confrontation resolutions
